observed.facings.png: Four facings at one shared scale. South: two small carved wooden post caps side by side, nothing else. East: a short ladder lying on a diagonal, its upper end to the right. It has two round pole stringers running roughly left-right, five round dowel rungs running up-down, rope lashings and metal end caps. North: a tall dark weathered ladder with plank rungs, X rope lashings, rusty iron plates and carved tops; it has a soft dark drop-shadow fringe. West: the east sprite mirrored.
observed.south.png: Two small (~27 px tall) dark-brown cylinder tops with carved, crown-like end grain and a rope band. They sit side by side in the lower middle of the canvas, with clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A small ladder in the lower-right of the canvas, rising toward the upper right. The stringers are round, light orange-tan poles with darker metal-banded ends. Five round rungs stand vertical between them, with rope wraps at the joints. Shading gives the poles a lit top and a shadowed underside, so they read as cylinders. It has a fairly heavy dark outline and is brighter and cleaner than the north art.
observed.north.png: The kept art: a front-on ladder with two square-ish dark weathered posts, five plank rungs, X rope lashings, rusty bolted plates and carved tops. The painterly texture is gritty, and a faint shadow halo surrounds it.
observed.west.png: A mirror of east, sitting in the lower-left of the canvas and rising to the upper left.
observed.scale.png: A pit outline with a human for scale. North: the ladder hangs over the far rim and down the far wall band. East: a short diagonal ladder with its top over the east rim line; it descends left across the light wall band and ends at about the edge of the dark pit floor. West: a mirror image on the west rim. South: two nubs on the near rim line. The human is far larger than the east/west ladders.
observed.wall_context.png: Same composite as scale.png: the pit with all four facings placed on their walls, plus the human.
observed.variants_1.png: Close crops against each wall. East: the ladder spans the black rim line, with its upper-right end on the outer ground and its lower-left foot on the light wall band, short of the dark floor. West: the mirror. South: two nubs straddling the near rim line. North: the kept ladder over the far wall.
observed.variants_2.png: A vanilla reference strip for WallTorch, WallLamp, AncientEmergencyLight, LifesupportUnit and OxygenPump in their north, east and south views. In the south views only a small cap or sliver shows, at the top of the cell.

CAMERA.seen: The E/W ladder rises toward its rim end, so its higher end draws further up the screen, which is consistent with the 35° camera. The poles show lit tops and shaded undersides.

BORE.seen: No pipe or hose. The pole ends are capped with carved or metal ends, and no hollow bore shows.

PORTS.seen: The card lists no ports and there is no assembled view; a ladder has no couplers.

WALL_LEAN.seen: East: the top is over the east rim (right) and the foot descends left onto the wall band. West: the mirror, with the top over the west rim. South: the nubs sit on the near rim. North: it hangs over the far rim. Each matches its wall side.

WALL_AXIS.seen: The east and west long axes run left-right (east-west) on a shallow diagonal, from the rim down into the pit. The stringers run left-right and the rungs up-down. North runs up/down the far face. South shows only the tops.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The card has no code ports, and no connector-like features are drawn.

LAYERS.seen: No assembled view and no attached parts.

ROTATIONS.seen: East and west are bright, clean orange-tan round poles with a heavier outline and round dowel rungs. North is dark, gritty, weathered plank-and-post with X lashings and rusty plates. Both are wooden lashed ladders, but the palette and surface finish read as a different artist.

SIGNATURE.seen: A wooden lashed ladder is recognisable on every facing. South shows the stringer tops, as the description asks.

MATERIAL.seen: Wood grain, rope wraps and metal bands read as materials. The east/west wood is a bit clean and saturated, but it is not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: All facings sit inside the 384 canvas. In context the east/west foot stops at about the edge of the dark pit floor and the top rests over the rim.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all facings; there is no backdrop under the new E/W/S art. North (kept) has a faint shadow fringe.

OURS.seen: These are mod-generated renders, not vanilla or donor art. The vanilla strip is reference only.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: E/W now run east-west (not north-south). They are 3D cylinders, not a flat compressed copy. They stay out of the dark pit. South is only small nubs, not a truncated north ladder.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell E/W read as a short slanted ladder (the rungs are distinct dark gaps). The south nubs are tiny by design, like the vanilla wall-attachment south views.

findings.seen: East/west are bright orange-tan, smooth round poles and dowel rungs with a heavy dark keyline. North is dark, gritty, weathered wood with plank rungs, X rope lashings and rusty bolted plates. Side by side they read as two different ladders or artists.
findings.quote: Rotations agree: same machine, same parts, same palette on every rotation.
findings.fix: The east and west ladders use the north facing's dark weathered wood tone, gritty painterly texture, X-pattern rope lashings and rusty iron plates, so all facings read as the same ladder.

findings.seen: The edges are cleaner, more saturated and more strongly outlined than the north art and vanilla painterly wood. They lean slightly toward a clean cel/illustration finish.
findings.quote: Painterly vanilla RimWorld … a clean dark outline that reads at standard zoom. Not toy-figurine cel shading, not heavy black keylines
findings.fix: The east and west ladders are rendered with soft painterly shading, a thinner outline and muted, weathered wood colour matching the north art.

findings.seen: The south nubs are dark and close-cropped, slightly wider than the north stringer tops. This is consistent in scale and only a minor mismatch.

reply.subject: RM_LadderPortable
reply.image_seen: 1: four wooden ladder facings on checkerboard; 2: two isolated south caps; 3: short, rounded east ladder; 4: tall, weathered north ladder; 5: mirrored west ladder; 6: facings around a pit beside a human; 7: matching wall composition; 8: enlarged wall compositions showing north, east, west and south.

concerns.evidence: In images 1, 3–5 and 8, east/west have bright honey-tan cylindrical rungs and smoothly rounded stringers. North has darker, rougher wood, broad plank-like rungs and more prominent rusty plates and crossed lashings. Both depict wooden ladders, but their construction and surface treatment visibly disagree.

East/west show uniformly crisp dark contours around golden poles and repeated clean highlights on the rungs. North has more broken, muted shading and irregular weathering. The side views still show wood grain and convincing thickness; the cleaner illustration finish is a polish concern rather than an unmistakably cartoon identity.

Images 1, 2 and 8 show two small south caps with spacing and individual widths comparable to the north stringer tops. Their much shorter visible height comes from the intended near-wall occlusion. There is no marked scale jump visible.
Images 3 and 5 show solid wooden end faces with grain and fastening details, not hollow pipe openings. No pipe or hose bore is depicted, so there is no visible BORE_PLANE violation.

The card defines zero ports. Across the isolated facings, the visible fittings are rope lashings and small fastening plates; no hose sockets, couplers or cord connectors appear. The drawings agree with the empty port list.

Images 6–8 show wall compositions, including the intended south-cap occlusion, but none is identified as the required assembled in-game capture. These panels cannot establish runtime draw-layer order. An assembled capture for each rotation is missing, which triggers the module's HOLD_INPUT requirement.
